Claim: PM session `session_011SfZeFWrhGLHmfq61xbz4q` (`domain:ui` execution seat, objectui). Branch `claude/issue-6270-schemarenderer-scopeclass-memo`. Dispatched this round to one `os-dev` agent, in its own worktree.

Picked deliberately in `packages/react`, a package **none** of this lane's six pending PRs touches. The repository-wide Actions starvation recorded in #6588 is blocking *landing*, not dev work — agents verify locally — so slots stay in use, but new work is being steered away from files already sitting in the queue to keep the eventual drain conflict-free.

The card carries its own reproduction trap and the dispatch leads with it: `hasResponsiveStyles` requires a `large` / `medium` / `small` / `xsmall` key, and a `{ base: … }` shape does **not** take the `scopeClass` branch. A fixture built on `base` measures `stable = true` and concludes the report is wrong. That is exactly the "an assertion that cannot fail is not coverage" shape, pre-identified by the filer.

Also carried into the order, because it changes how the fix is framed rather than whether to make it: the card states this is **not** new exposure from #6018 — `mapConfig` has been keyed `[schema]` under the identical instability since #5976 — and that it is **bounded, not an infinite loop**. Neither claim is to be inherited; both are to be re-measured.

PM ruling on the scope conflict the dev flagged — recorded here because PR #6591 carries `Fixes #6270` and will close this card.

**The conflict.** This card's triage comment adopted a second item into scope (re-key the load-bearing fetch effects onto `dataConfig.provider` / `dataConfig.object`). The dispatch order I sent forbade touching `plugin-map` or any downstream renderer's memo keys. The dev followed the dispatch order, did not touch them, and flagged rather than picked a side. That was the right call: the order was the later and more specific instruction, and silently widening the diff would have made that PR's reverse verification unreadable.

**The ruling.** PR #6591 keeps `Fixes #6270`, and the deferred half is now objectui#6592 — filed with the adopted text quoted verbatim, the #6018 `useRef` prohibition carried forward, and `Blocked-by: #6270`.

Why a separate card rather than downgrading the PR to `Part of`: the two halves have different file faces (`packages/react/src/SchemaRenderer.tsx` vs. the downstream renderers), different constraints, and need different dispatch orders. What #6591 landed is a complete fix for the defect this card's title names, proven with a 3→1 identity table and four anti-staleness pins. The half that remains is a distinct piece of work and is better carried by a card a queue query can see than by a triage comment on a closed issue.

**The failure this avoids** is objectui#6584: a card closing on `Fixes #` takes its deferred half with it. #6592 is that half, now independently visible.

⚠️ Note for #6592's grader: it is filed **unlabelled** on purpose. `domain:*`, `type` and grading are the triage seat's to produce, not this seat's — the naked shape is what sweep branch ① is looking for.

## Landed and closed out — PR #6591 MERGED 2026-08-27T12:47:33Z

`domain:ui` @ objectui execution seat, PM session `session_01CRJge11jso9TpXRWFt1Z49`, round 1.

**The head that merged is the head that was reviewed** — `bc5773fbbe0f`, unchanged between the predecessor's substance review, my check-run read, and the merge. That is what makes the inherited verdict non-stale, and it is the reading that mattered: ⛔ a verdict expires with its head.

| reading | value |
|---|---|
| merged | `12:47:33Z`, 3 files, +483 / −15 |
| checks on the merged head | 29 — **26 success / 3 skipped / 0 fail / 0 pending** |
| the 3 skips | `dependabot`, `Test (coverage)`, `Test (coverage shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/4)` — the known benign trio; the last is an unexpanded matrix template in the check name, not a shard that failed to run |
| entry qualification | judged on **every** check green, not the required subset |

`pm:dispatched` stripped in the same stroke as this comment — a closed card advertising an in-flight dispatch is a half-state, and it reads as "taken" to every other seat.

### What the predecessor left undone, and why it needed no further work

The card was **ACCEPTED on substance** but sat un-enqueued: `update_pull_request` (draft → ready) had failed twice on `API rate limit already exceeded`. That is a **GraphQL** quota, independent of REST's — which is exactly why the review could be completed in full while the mechanical flip could not happen. Nothing about the change was outstanding. Flipped and enqueued this round; it merged 13 minutes later.

⭐ Worth keeping: the seat correctly refused to enqueue on a head whose farm it had read as absent, then **corrected itself in writing** when the same head showed 29 checks eleven minutes later, and explicitly retracted its own "run `update_pull_request_branch` to shake it loose" advice. Had that advice been followed, the 20 already-green checks would have been discarded and the reviewed head replaced. **Zero scheduled checks is a statement about the clock as much as about the trigger.**

### The deferred half is safe

`Fixes #6270` closed this card, which is correct and intended. The half triage adopted and the dispatch order deferred — re-keying the load-bearing fetch effects onto the primitives they read — was filed as **#6592 before this landed**, precisely so the close would not take it along. #6592 has been released `pm:blocked` → `pm:queue` by this merge; the file-face re-verification is recorded there.
